name: Bank of Maharashtra
title: Bank of Maharashtra - 532525 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: FY26 met every guidance item with margin: NIM 3.91% vs 3.75% guide, GNPA 1.45%, NNPA 0.13%, but FY27 guidance is held roughly flat and a West Asia stress is flagged for Q2 onward.

triggers.label: NIM 3.91% vs 3.75% guide
triggers.quote: Against a NIM guidance of 3.75% at the beginning of the year, we closed the year with a NIM of 3.91%.

triggers.label: Gross NPA 1.45%, down 29 bps
triggers.quote: The gross NPA has reached -- percentage come down to 1.45% with a 29 bps improvement year -on-year.

triggers.label: West Asia stress from Q2 flagged
triggers.quote: By Q2, you will see the fallout of the West Asia crisis.

triggers.label: FY27 credit cost ~1%, GNPA within 2%
triggers.quote: GNPA will remain within 2%. NNPA within 0.25%. Slippage will be maintained below 1%, and credit cost will be around 1%.

triggers.label: Gold loan book fell QoQ on CLM1 shift
triggers.quote: we did not do any fresh underwriting till the time we switched on from the CLM2 to CLM1 model

guidance.quote: ROA, here, we have actually upped our guidance number by 5 bps.

noninterest income, if you are -- you must have seen, it is 2.51%, whereas we have kept 10% guidance for this year.

summary.headline: Bank of Maharashtra FY26: net profit INR7,019 crore (+27% YoY), full-year NIM 3.91%, ROA 1.86%, all guidance met; FY27 ROA guidance 1.80%.
summary.overview: Management reported that all FY26 guidance metrics were met, several with headroom, with total business up 17% and advances up 22% YoY. Gross NPA fell 29 bps to 1.45% and net NPA to 0.13%, while operating profit rose 16% to INR10,826 crore. Management created an INR200 crore "global geopolitical uncertainties" provision in Q4 as a buffer against the West Asia crisis, and said stress is not yet visible in MSME. Non-interest income was weak (2.51% growth) due to a one-time INR290 crore MTM hit from the RRB amalgamation. FY27 guidance was issued across 18-19 parameters, with ROA lifted to 1.80%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew 32% YoY; home loans +29%, vehicle loans +56%, gold loans +53% to INR24,000 crore, of which about INR5,000 crore is co-lent with NBFCs. Retail slippages in Q4 were about INR100 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew 22% YoY, with RAM split 63:37 (retail/agri/MSME vs corporate). Corporate reported no slippages in Q4; INR72,000 crore sanctioned in FY26 with INR34,500 crore undisbursed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 11% YoY (about INR6,000 crore added per management); MSME NPA fell to 1.54%. Q4 MSME slippages were about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri grew 13% YoY; agri NPA was 7.72% (about INR3,100 crore). Q4 agri slippages were about INR300 crore.

segments.name: GIFT City IBU
segments.commentary: Overseas advances rose to INR6,142 crore from INR3,517 crore (2% of book). Management said the IBU turned profitable in March after covering all overheads; 650 million USD booked against a 1 billion USD 12-month aspiration.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve swung from +INR175 crore in Q3 to -INR362 crore at 31 March; FVTPL MTM gain of about INR40-45 crore booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total business growth 16-17%; advances 18%; deposits 14-15%; CASA around 50%.
RAM growth 18% with RAM corporate mix at 60:40 (+/-2%); non-interest income growth 10%; NII growth 15%.
FY27 NIM guidance 3.75%; cost to income below 40%; ROA 1.80%; ROE 20% or more.
GNPA within 2%, NNPA within 0.25%, slippage below 1%, credit cost around 1%, PCR around 98%, CRAR maintained at 18%.
Management expects FY27 tax at about 10% of PBT (OP tax rate 13-14%), with PBT-basis tax about 18-20%, after unabsorbed losses of about INR1,200-1,300 crore were used up in Q1.
Debt waiver: about INR2,000 crore expected (INR917 crore overdue + INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts), with approval expected Q2 to Q3 FY27; agri NPA could fall to about 5.33%.
capex_capacity: Project 321: 321 new branches in the first 3-year phase, 183 functional to date; Board has approved 1,000 branches over 5 years.
GIFT City IBU: first business booked September 2025; retail products planned for H2 FY27.
PLI for Scale 4 and above not yet released; 100% provision made, release pending discussions.
demand_pricing: Management expects West Asia crisis impact to show from Q2 FY27 rather than Q1, with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk; no MSME stress seen as of March.
Q4 SMA-1 was INR241 crore and SMA-2 INR56 crore as of 31 March (per analyst).
Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises, but gave no specific pricing action.
Pool/assignment book of about INR14,000 crore is largely lent to AA/AAA NBFCs; security cover is low as it is pool-based.
Gold co-lending slowed after RBI's CLM1 guidelines from 1 January 2026; fresh underwriting resumed in early March, with 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the West Asia war affect corporate and MSME accounts from April onward, and what stress is visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress was visible in March and MSME NPA fell to 1.54%, but impact is expected from Q2 FY27 and depends on how long the crisis lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the special provision fall to INR1,010 crore from INR1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the COVID buffer was released, and a new INR200 crore global geopolitical uncertainties provision was built in Q4, with no regulatory prescription behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time non-interest income drag?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR290 crore MTM provision was taken on investments in the RRB (Vidharbha Konkan Gramin Bank) that was amalgamated into a single Maharashtra RRB, with the bank as sponsor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net worth fall QoQ and gold loans drop about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth fell due to AFS reserve movement and dividends (interim 10% plus final 12%, about INR1,692 crore total). Gold loans dropped because fresh underwriting paused during the shift from CLM2 to CLM1 co-lending; underwriting resumed in early March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is on the normal tax rate from Q2 FY26, with OP tax at 13-14%. FY27 PBT-basis tax is expected around 18-20%, and the call gave a 10% figure for the tax on PBT in the same answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split of Q4 slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail about INR100 crore, agri about INR300 crore, MSME about INR400 crore, and corporate nil.

risks_watch: West Asia / crude-driven stress in MSME and corporate books from Q2 FY27; a 1.2% to 2% geopolitical provision top-up is open.
Timing and size of the state KCC debt waiver (about INR2,000 crore); the scheme is not yet approved.
Tax-rate normalisation to about 25% creates an earnings headwind; management guided FY27 PBT-basis tax at 18-20%, but the figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Non-interest income growth (2.51% in FY26) versus 10% target; a fee-income push is planned for FY27.
Gold co-lending volume recovery after CLM1 transition; the book fell about 17% QoQ.
Pending PLI payout for Scale 4 and above, and the NCLT recovery pipeline (about INR7,500 crore in NCLT).
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, with management calling the targets "sacrosanct". Cautious and somewhat evasive on the West Asia impact, saying the full effect cannot yet be gauged and that the crisis is not over.
key_quotes: we have been able to meet all the guidance and at some of the places with a decent margin above the guidance that was shared in the beginning of the year.
These are sacrosanct numbers for us. We will be achieving itself.
So we can only hope that the crisis resolves and what damage must have happened, the impact, how fast it can be replaced is also needs to be seen.

adds.what: Project 321: 321 new branches in first 3-year phase (183 functional to date); Board approved 1,000 branches over 5 years

growth.why: FY27 total business growth guided at 16-17% (advances 18%, deposits 14-15%, NII 15%), backed by partial specifics: 183 of 321 Project 321 branches functional, 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed and gold co-lending restarting, but no concrete order or capacity numbers tied to the 18% advances target.
